rounds.text: Active Infrastructure Ltd demonstrates superior capital efficiency relative to its peers, evidenced by a strong return on assets of 4.95% compared to the sector benchmark of 1.64% [E8], and a higher return on equity of 8.85% against the sector benchmark of 4.26% [E9]. Furthermore, the company exhibits a solid multi-year earnings quality profile, maintaining a 5-year median return on equity of 16% [E19]. Operational profitability has also expanded over the medium term, with the operating margin reaching 17% in March 2026, marking a two percentage point improvement from three years prior [E22]. Demonstrating strong operational momentum, recent screens highlight robust sales performance with year-over-year sales growth of 23% alongside quarter-on-quarter increases [E48, E50]. Finally, management exhibits unwavering commitment and skin in the game, as promoter shareholding increased by 1.95 percentage points to reach 73.31% by June 2026 [E34]. Conceded: [E28], [E37], [E46].

Active Infrastructure Ltd carries severe fundamental and valuation risks, starting with a severe cash flow crisis where operating cash flow plunged to Rs -25 Cr and free cash flow reached Rs -65 Cr in Mar 2026 [E27, E28]. This deterioration is underscored by a cash conversion ratio of -2.50x and operating cash flow at -107% of operating profit, alongside rising borrowings of Rs 80 Cr and alarming operational friction visible in working capital days surging from 126 to 259 days and high debtors of 189 days [E26, E29, E32, E45, E46]. Valuation metrics compound these fundamental cracks: the stock trades at a P/E of 25.4x and P/B of 2.14x, exceeding sector benchmarks, while a discounted cash flow model suggests the market price of Rs 172 drastically outpaces intrinsic value and implies an aggressive 11.8% earnings growth against a base case of just 1.0% [E1, E2, E6, E7, E37, E39]. Furthermore, profitability momentum is fading as evidenced by a quarterly operating margin collapse of -13 percentage points year-over-year in Mar 2026, a 3-year compounded profit growth of a meager 1%, and explicit flags regarding potential interest cost capitalization and low multi-year return on equity [E16, E23, E43, E44, E51]. Conceded: promoters increased their holding to 73.31% (+1.95 percentage points) and return on assets and ROCE outperform sector benchmarks [E8, E10, E34].

Conceded: operating cash flow reached Rs -25 Cr, free cash flow hit Rs -65 Cr, cash conversion stood at -2.50x, operating cash flow was -107% of operating profit, borrowings rose to Rs 80 Cr, working capital days increased to 259, debtors reached 189 days, and a DCF suggests an intrinsic value of Rs 79 [E26, E27, E28, E29, E32, E37, E45, E46]. Despite these cash flow and working capital strains, the company's operating margin expanded by 2 percentage points over three years to 17% in March 2026, demonstrating underlying core operational resilience [E22]. Furthermore, the bear overstates valuation concerns by ignoring that the company's EV/EBITDA of 14.83x is actually more attractive than the sector benchmark of 15.54x [E11]. While the bear highlights lagging multi-year profit growth, recent performance shows momentum with compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months at 8%, alongside robust sales acceleration of 23% YoY [E16, E17, E48]. Crucially, the bear's claim of fading commitment is refuted by insiders, as promoters demonstrated ultimate confidence by increasing their holding by 1.95 percentage points to 73.31% [E34]. Finally, efficiency metrics such as return on assets of 4.95% strongly outpace the sector benchmark of 1.64%, proving the business extracts superior value from its assets than its peers [E8].

Conceded: EV/EBITDA of 14.83x sits below the sector benchmark of 15.54x, ROA of 4.95% outpaces the sector's 1.64%, promoters increased holdings by 1.95 percentage points to 73.31%, and sales grew 23% YoY [E8, E11, E34, E48]. However, citing trailing 12-month profit growth of 8% ignores the structural reality of a stagnant 3-year compounded profit growth of just 1% [E16, E17]. Furthermore, the bull minimizes severe operational deterioration by dismissing a quarterly operating margin collapse from 25% down to 12% in Mar 2026 (-13 percentage points) and an inconsistent annual operating-margin trend [E23, E24, E25]. The bull's dismissal of cash burn is untenable when operating cash flow hit an alarming Rs -25 Cr alongside a free cash flow deficit of Rs -65 Cr, directly driving borrowings up to Rs 80 Cr [E27, E28, E32]. Finally, this cash drain is compounded by extreme working capital distress, with debtor days ballooning to 189 and overall working capital days surging from 126 to 259 [E45, E46].
